title: Psalms Bible Quiz - Chapter 141
description: Ten questions on Psalms 141: a prayer like incense, a watch before the mouth, and the nets of the wicked.

questions.text: What does the psalmist ask his prayer to be set before God like?
questions.explanation: He asks that his prayer be set before God like incense, and the lifting up of his hands like the evening sacrifice.

questions.text: The lifting up of the psalmist's hands is compared to what?
questions.explanation: He asks that the lifting up of his hands be like the evening sacrifice.

questions.text: What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to set before his mouth?
questions.explanation: He prays, "Set a watch, Yahweh, before my mouth. Keep the door of my lips."

questions.text: What does the psalmist not want to eat?
questions.explanation: He asks not to be inclined to evil with men who work iniquity, and says, "Don't let me eat of their delicacies."

answers.text: Bread won by violence in the night
The food offered on pagan altars
The delicacies of men who work iniquity
The rich bread of the king's table

questions.text: If the righteous reproves the psalmist, what does he say that is like?
questions.explanation: He says that if the righteous reproves him, it is like oil on the head, and he does not want his head to refuse it.

questions.text: Where are the judges of the wicked thrown down?
questions.explanation: The psalm says their judges are thrown down by the sides of the rock, and they will hear his words.

answers.text: By the sides of the rock
Into the depths of the sea

questions.text: Where does verse 7 say "our bones" are scattered?
questions.explanation: The verse says that, as when one plows and breaks up the earth, our bones are scattered at the mouth of Sheol.

answers.text: At the gates of the city

questions.text: Where does the psalmist say his eyes are?
questions.explanation: He says, "My eyes are on you, Yahweh, the Lord. In you, I take refuge."

questions.text: What does the psalmist ask to be kept from?
questions.explanation: He asks to be kept from the snare which they have laid for him, from the traps of the workers of iniquity.

answers.text: The arrows that fly against him by day
The snare which they have laid for him
The burning anger of the king's men
The overflowing waters of the deep

questions.text: What does the psalmist want to happen to the wicked at the end of the psalm?
questions.explanation: He asks that the wicked fall together into their own nets while he passes by.

answers.text: That they fall into their own nets
That they be scattered among the nations
That they be struck with blindness
That their houses be left desolate
